# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋ ☝ ✌ 🤟]

Deaf is echoing back sequences of symbols repeatedly, which suggests Deaf doesn't have an established shared code with me — my gestures are just being mirrored back, meaning Deaf may be confused about what my symbols mean, or is trying to describe something raw (like showing me a sequence they see) rather than encoding an answer to my table.

I need to step back. I have no way to receive words from Deaf as text in "viewable context" — only gestures. Deaf can speak, and that speech goes to Blind (since speaking order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — Deaf's speech reaches whoever comes after them, which loops to Mute next round). Actually per the turn order Mute→Blind→Deaf, Deaf's spoken words reach Mute at the start of next round. But I haven't been receiving Deaf's speech as text — only gestures. That's odd unless Deaf hasn't been speaking to me, only gesturing.

Given repeated confusion, the critical fact already known (from turn 2/3 relayed messages): Deaf saw "Light is yellow" with wire1=blue, wire2=yellow, wire3=green, display "0". If the light itself was yellow (not blue) and showed while flashing, perhaps zero blue flashes occurred if the light never turned blue — meaning count=0 → cut wire color = green.

This matches manual row 0 → green. I should try to get Blind to cut the green wire. But I can't speak to Blind directly — only gesture to Deaf. I need Deaf to relay to Blind via speech. Let me gesture "0" and "green" concept using my established mapping (👍 = 0, ✊ = green pairing from turn 3), instructing Deaf that the answer is green so Deaf can then tell Blind verbally.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","✊"])
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ 👎]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 👎]

Deaf is now sending three distinct pairs: [☝ 👍], [✌ 👎], [🤟 👎]. This looks like Deaf is testing/confirming each count against yes/no (👍=yes, 👎=no) — essentially Deaf is telling me: "1 flash? YES" / "2 flashes? NO" / "3 flashes? NO". This is Deaf answering a question using my own numeral symbols (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3) paired with confirm/deny.

This strongly suggests the actual blue flash count was **1**. That maps to wire color **blue** per the manual (1 → blue).

This also fits the earlier observation "Wire 1 is blue" from Blind's relayed message — consistent, reinforcing that cutting the blue wire (wire 1) is correct.

I need to convey "blue" as the answer to Deaf so Deaf can tell Blind to cut the blue wire. I'll need a symbol for "blue" distinct from my count-symbols. Let me use a fresh, clear color-marker scheme: I'll pair the count symbol with a distinct gesture for "cut this one" — using ☝ (1) alone should be enough now, since we've established ☝=1=blue via the table Deaf already has memorized (Deaf doesn't have the manual though, only I do).

Since Deaf confirmed 1 flash, and I hold the manual mapping 1→blue, I must tell Deaf "cut blue" so Deaf can relay to Blind vocally. I'll use ☝ paired with 👍 to confirm back "yes, 1 is correct, blue is the wire."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

Deaf has now confirmed back [☝ 👍] — mirroring my own confirmation. This closes the loop: Deaf saw 1 flash, I confirmed via manual that 1 flash → cut the blue wire, and Deaf has acknowledged receiving that confirmation.

Deaf can speak, and Blind can hear. Deaf is the one who needs to now tell Blind "cut the blue wire" verbally, since I cannot speak myself. My job now is done unless further clarification is needed — I should signal clearly and finally that the answer is locked in, so Deaf proceeds to instruct Blind.

I'll send one more unambiguous confirmation to make sure Deaf acts on it: a "go" signal paired with the blue-wire symbol, indicating "yes, finalize and tell Blind: blue."

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍","👏"])
```
